classification.difficultyReason: Model five end-of-year deposits as a geometric series, then calculate the shortfall against a savings target.

content.prompt:
Liam wants to save up $\$15\,000$ for a car in 5 years’ time.

He invests $\$2000$ at the end of each year in an account that pays 7.5% p.a. interest.

How much more will Liam have to pay at the end of 5 years to make up the $\$15\,000$? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
End of 1st year: $2000$

End of 2nd year: $2000(1.075)+2000$

End of 5th year: $2000(1.075)^4+2000(1.075)^3+\cdots+2000$

This is a geometric series with $a=2000$, common ratio $R=1.075$ and $n=5$.

$$\begin{aligned}FV&=\frac{2000(1.075^5-1)}{1.075-1}\\FV&=11616.78203125\end{aligned}$$

Amount still needed:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Shortfall}&=15000-11616.78203125\\\text{Shortfall}&=3383.21796875\\\text{Shortfall}&\approx\$3383.22\end{aligned}$$
